learning: Iteration 0 showed line loss preceding off-track on every track, so the sensing footprint is the first lever. The kp increase is my compensation for the wider array and is untested. If steering_oscillation rises with no line loss, the gain or forward offset is the next thing to check.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's seven-sensor span proposal, with antisymmetric weights matched to sensor x and kp raised to 4.0 to offset the flatter signal scale. All other geometry is unchanged so the race isolates the span effect.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials with zero completions. All ended off_track, with line_loss_events of 1.0 to 1.8, max_error at 0.061 to 0.064 m (just past the 0.06 m limit), and progress of 0.11 to 0.22. Line loss precedes every off-track failure, so the controller's first job is to keep the tape in view. The Builder's proposal widens the array to seven 12 mm sensors at 12 mm pitch (x = -0.036 to +0.036 m, y = 0.03 m). I keep all other geometry as proposed, because the Builder is isolating the span effect. Sensor weights are antisymmetric and proportional to x, scaled so the outermost sensors carry +/-1.0: [-1.0, -0.667, -0.333, 0, 0.333, 0.667, 1.0]. Positive x is left of centre and gives a positive weight, which steers left as the contract requires. Because the outer weights now sit at 0.036 m instead of 0.024 m, the signal changes about 33 percent less per millimetre of lateral error. I raise kp from 3.0 to 4.0 to offset that flatter scale, which keeps the steering authority near iteration 0's level. ki stays at 0.05 to avoid windup on the long bends, and kd stays at 0.3 for damping, since iteration 0 showed oscillation of 0.14 to 0.16 with no evidence yet that it needs more. base_speed stays at 1.5, which gives the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s. line_loss stays at last_direction, which turns toward the side the tape was last seen and is the best recovery available on bends. I expect line_loss_events to fall toward zero on the s-bend and slalom and max_error to fall below 0.06 m. I cannot verify this before the race.
